cve_summary: drivers/net/can/usb/gs_usb.c in the Linux kernel 4.9.x and 4.10.x before 4.10.2 interacts incorrectly with the CONFIG_VMAP_STACK option, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (system crash or memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging use of more than one virtual page for a DMA scatterlist.
commit_message:
can: gs_usb: Don't use stack memory for USB transfers

Fixes: 05ca5270005c can: gs_usb: add ethtool set_phys_id callback to locate physical device

The gs_usb driver is performing USB transfers using buffers allocated on
the stack. This causes the driver to not function with vmapped stacks.
Instead, allocate memory for the transfer buffers.

Signed-off-by: Ethan Zonca <e@ethanzonca.com>
Cc: linux-stable <stable@vger.kernel.org> # >= v4.8
Signed-off-by: Marc Kleine-Budde <mkl@pengutronix.de>
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Initializes a USB device by probing the USB interface and configuring it based on the device's capabilities.

Parameters: 
intf (struct usb_interface *): Pointer to the USB interface to be probed.
id (const struct usb_device_id *): Pointer to the USB device ID structure.

Returns: 
int: Returns 0 on success, or a negative error code on failure.

Logic: 
The function allocates memory for host and device configurations, sends a control message to set the host format, and retrieves the device configuration. It checks the number of interfaces supported and initializes the device structure. If any allocation or control message fails, it cleans up allocated resources and returns an error code. The function also creates CAN devices for each interface and handles errors during their creation.
"""
extraction_reason: vulnerable-side scope spans 2 top-level constructs (functions/declarations), not a single function
